William Greenhill
WIL-yuhm GREEN-hil
proper noun
From the surname Greenhill (dweller by a green hill); borne by a Westminster divine famed for his exposition of Ezekiel.

Biblical Definition

William Greenhill was a divine of the Westminster Assembly, an Independent by conviction and a faithful pastor, whose life-labour was a vast and searching exposition of the prophecy of Ezekiel, opened chapter by chapter with great care and spiritual profit. In that dark book of visions and woes he traced the glory of the LORD departing from a polluted temple and returning again to a temple restored, the watchman set to warn the wicked from his way (Eze 3:17), the valley of dry bones made to live by the breath of the Spirit (Eze 37), and the sure promise of a new heart and a new spirit given to God’s covenant people. Greenhill taught that the God who threatens judgment upon impenitent men also swears He hath no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live (Eze 33:11). The dictionary honours Greenhill as a diligent expositor who fed the flock upon the whole counsel of God, refusing to pass by the harder prophets, and who pressed upon his hearers the watchman’s solemn charge to warn, and the gospel promise that the LORD Himself will give a heart of flesh in place of the heart of stone.

A Westminster divine and Independent pastor, famed for his exposition of Ezekiel.

Key Scripture

Eze 3:17 — "Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me."

Eze 33:11 — "Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?"

Eze 36:26 — "A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh."

Eze 37:5 — "Thus saith the Lord GOD unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live:"

Modern Corruption

A faithful expositor, not a contested doctrine; his life recovers the principle of preaching the whole counsel of God.

expand to see more

Greenhill is preserved because his life was given to opening a difficult prophet whom lesser men neglect, feeding the flock upon the whole counsel of God rather than the easy portions only. His Ezekiel labours the watchman’s solemn charge to warn and the sovereign promise of a new heart, keeping both the terror and the tenderness of God before the reader.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the diligent, unabridged exposition of Scripture — that the pastor must warn the wicked from his way as a watchman answerable for blood, and must proclaim the covenant mercy whereby the LORD takes away the stony heart and gives a heart of flesh. Regeneration is here shown to be God’s own act, dry bones raised by His breath alone, that no man may boast; and this Greenhill preached faithfully, sparing neither the woe nor the wonder of the vision.

"The watchman must give warning from the LORD, else the blood is required at his hand."
